historical_timeline.summary: Polio at age six, leaving the right leg thinner and shorter.
Bus struck by a streetcar: pelvic, spinal, collarbone, rib, and right leg fractures.
Began to paint while immobilized in bed.
Chronic pain, many operations, and about 25 corsets.
Stopped attending her classes at La Esmeralda because of limited mobility.
Nearly a year in hospital with an infection after a spinal graft.
Right leg amputated below the knee for threatened gangrene.
Died at the Blue House, aged 47.

claims.statement: Magdalena Carmen Frida Kahlo Calderón was born on July 6, 1907, in her parents' house in Coyoacán, Mexico City, now known as the Blue House, the daughter of Guillermo Kahlo and Matilde Calderón.
Frida Kahlo died at the Blue House in Mexico City on July 13, 1954, at the age of 47.
claims.clinical_interpretation: Record the death as a fact without graphic detail.

claims.statement: In 1913, at the age of six, Kahlo fell ill with polio; afterward her right leg was thinner, slightly shorter, and less developed, with the foot turned outward, and her father encouraged cycling and swimming.
claims.clinical_interpretation: The contemporaneous diagnosis was polio; a retrospective analysis adds a congenital spinal anomaly.

claims.statement: A neurologist's retrospective review proposes that Kahlo also had a congenital spinal anomaly (spina bifida).
claims.clinical_interpretation: Retrospective interpretation; kept off the active problem list.

claims.statement: On September 17, 1925, at 18, Kahlo was riding a bus that was struck by a streetcar; a metal handrail impaled her through the hip and fractured her pelvis, and she had three fractures of the spinal column, a fractured collarbone, two rib fractures, a dislocated right shoulder, and eleven fractures of the right leg with a dislocated foot.
claims.clinical_interpretation: The documented injuries behind the synthetic chronic pain diagnoses; stated without graphic detail.

source_links.locator: Abstract: a horrific trolley car accident in her teens

claims.statement: While immobilized for several months after the accident, Kahlo began to paint, using an easel adapted for painting in bed.
claims.clinical_interpretation: A documented strength: art as a way through prolonged pain and bed rest.

claims.statement: Kahlo lived with chronic pain for the rest of her life, underwent many operations, some with long convalescences and serious consequences, and used about 25 different corsets.

source_links.locator: Abstract: lifelong chronic pain and numerous failed spinal surgeries

claims.statement: In 1944, because of increasingly limited mobility, Kahlo had to stop attending her classes at the La Esmeralda school of painting and sculpture, and some students continued to work with her at the Blue House.
claims.clinical_interpretation: The documented functional decline that anchors the index age.

claims.statement: Her pain has been interpreted retrospectively as including chronic neuropathic pain and central sensitization.
claims.clinical_interpretation: Modern pain-science interpretation; informs the synthetic multimodal plan.

claims.statement: In 1950 Kahlo spent nearly the whole year in hospital with an infection after a graft to her spinal column.
In 1953 Kahlo's right leg was amputated below the knee because of the threat of gangrene.
Kahlo's father, Guillermo Kahlo, had epilepsy and died in 1941; her mother, Matilde Calderón, died in 1932.
claims.clinical_interpretation: The cited source does not give causes of death.

synthetic_episode.teaching_objective: Manage chronic pain after major trauma and childhood polio in a patient already on long-term opioid therapy, following the CDC 2022 opioid guideline: measure pain and function, build a nonopioid and rehabilitation plan, offer naloxone and other risk mitigation, and taper gradually and collaboratively rather than abruptly, while screening mood and treating post-traumatic ankle osteoarthritis on the CMID schedule.
